properties.areaDesc: Death Valley National Park
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 8 at 11:59PM PDT until October 12 at 5:00AM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Extreme Heat Warning, dangerously hot conditions
with heat index values up to 100. For the Wind Advisory, south
winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Death Valley National Park.

* WHEN...For the Extreme Heat Warning, until 8 PM PDT Friday. For the
Wind Advisory, from 2 PM Saturday to 5 AM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result. Heat
related illnesses increase significantly during extreme heat and
high humidity events.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 8 at 11:55PM PDT until October 12 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...A moderate risk for sneaker waves is expected.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...From early Sunday morning through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Avoid climbing on rocks and jetties. Stay away from the ocean and
remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

properties.areaDesc: Cherokee, IA; O'Brien, IA; Plymouth, IA; Sioux, IA
properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 9 at 1:53AM CDT until October 9 at 2:45AM CDT by NWS Sioux Falls SD
properties.description:
SVRFSD

The National Weather Service in Sioux Falls has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Cherokee County in northwestern Iowa...
Southwestern O'Brien County in northwestern Iowa...
Northeastern Plymouth County in northwestern Iowa...
Southeastern Sioux County in northwestern Iowa...

* Until 245 AM CDT.

* At 153 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 6 miles northeast
of Remsen, or 11 miles southeast of Orange City, moving east at 30
mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect damage
to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles.

* This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Granville around 200 AM CDT.
Marcus around 205 AM CDT.
Cleghorn around 215 AM CDT.
Paullina around 220 AM CDT.

Other locations impacted by the severe thunderstorm include Meriden.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing large hail.

Report severe weather to your nearest law enforcement agency or the
National Weather Service office in Sioux Falls SD.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 9 at 1:50AM CDT until October 11 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to
7 feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM CDT Saturday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM CDT Sunday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Max inundation will occur near high tide
cycles each afternoon.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Gallatin National Forest; Wheatland County/Sweet Grass County; Beartooth Ranger District Custer National Forest; Sheridan County/Casper BLM; Bighorn National Forest
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 9 at 12:48AM MDT until October 9 at 9:00PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
* IMPACTS: Low humidities, unseasonably warm temperatures, and
strong gusty winds will create erratic fire behavior and rapid
spread for new or existing fires.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In North Central WY Fire Zones...274...284.
In South Central MT Fire Zones...123...124...126.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In Central MT...Wheatland.
In North Central WY...Big Horn...Johnson...Sheridan...Washakie.
In South Central MT...Carbon...Park...Stillwater...Sweet Grass.
In Southwest MT...Gallatin.

* WIND: Southwest 15 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 7 percent.

* TEMPERATURES: 84 to 90 degrees, warmest over Zone WY274.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS: The worst conditions are expected across the
lower to middle elevations in fine fuels. The strongest winds are
expected in mountain locations and the foothills west of
Billings. Zone WY274 will see lower wind gusts of 15 to 25 mph.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute
to extreme fire behavior.

River Valley/Southern Sawtooth NF/Twin Falls BLM south of the
Snake River.

properties.instruction:

are either occurring now, or will shortly based on these criteria
for Southeastern Idaho:

- Relative humidity at or below 15 percent and wind gusts of at
least 25 mph in the mountains, or 30 mph in the Snake Plain.

- Thunderstorm coverage of 25 percent, without specific rainfall
criteria.

- Other high impact events deemed critical by the National
Weather Service and area fire management agencies.

properties.areaDesc: Lafayette; Inland Dixie; Coastal Dixie; Berrien; Lowndes; Lanier
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 9 at 2:37AM EDT until October 10 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Big Bend Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Dixie, Inland Dixie and Lafayette and south central
Georgia, including the following areas, Berrien, Lanier and
Lowndes.

* WHEN...From 2 PM EDT this afternoon through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Hurricane Isaias is expected to bring bands of heavy rainfall to
the area. Widespread totals of 4 to 8 inches are expected with
localized amounts of 10 to 15 inches. Given saturated soils from
recent heavy rainfall, flash flooding is expected. Considerable
flash flooding is possible where bands of heavy rain move
repeatedly over the same area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Suwannee; Baker; Inland Nassau; Union; Bradford; Gilchrist; Eastern Hamilton; Coastal Nassau; Coastal Duval; Eastern Clay; Eastern Alachua; Western Hamilton; Trout River; Western Clay; Western Alachua; Northern Columbia; South Central Duval; Southeastern Columbia; Western Duval; Southwestern Columbia
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 9 at 2:26AM EDT until October 10 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of northeast and northern Florida, including the
following areas, in northeast Florida, Baker, Coastal Duval,
Coastal Nassau, Eastern Clay, Inland Nassau, South Central Duval,
Trout River, Western Clay and Western Duval. In northern Florida,
Bradford, Eastern Alachua, Eastern Hamilton, Gilchrist, Northern
Columbia, Southeastern Columbia, Southwestern Columbia, Suwannee,
Union, Western Alachua and Western Hamilton.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A lifting warm front and moisture due to Hurricane Isaias passing
west of the area will bring waves of moderate to heavy rainfall
across areas of Northeast Florida today into this evening.
Several inches of rain from the last several days will make for
saturated soils and additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
with locally higher amounts may lead to flash flooding. The heavy
rainfall may combine with higher than normal tidal levels and may
worsen flood problems in some St. Johns River locations.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE TONIGHT
